qc.label_under_test: sentence-initial 'Thus' (and more weakly 'Hence') that draws a conclusion from the previous sentence, as against other sentence-initial connectives and mid-sentence 'thus'

neighbours.label: 'Thus' or 'Hence' starting a sentence in formal prose, and an unspaced dash opening an aside after a noun; not 'Therefore', 'However', 'Moreover' or spaced hyphens
fire: The samples were contaminated during transport. Thus the results of the second trial must be discarded.
Hence the committee recommends that the proposal be deferred until the next fiscal year.
The function is continuous on a closed interval. Hence it attains both a maximum and a minimum.
Thus, the court concluded that the contract had been validly formed.
Demand for grain fell sharply after the harvest. Thus prices in the regional markets declined for three consecutive months.
Hence, any solution to the equation must also satisfy the boundary condition.
The manuscript—long thought lost in the fire of 1731—was rediscovered in a private library.
The treaty—signed under considerable pressure—failed to secure a lasting peace.
quiet: The samples were contaminated during transport. Therefore the results of the second trial must be discarded.
Moreover, the committee recommends that the proposal be deferred until the next fiscal year.
The function is continuous on a closed interval, so it attains both a maximum and a minimum.
However, the court concluded that the contract had been validly formed.
Demand for grain fell sharply after the harvest, and prices in the regional markets declined for three consecutive months.
Therefore, any solution to the equation must also satisfy the boundary condition.
The manuscript - long thought lost in the fire of 1731 - was rediscovered in a private library.
The treaty, signed under considerable pressure, failed to secure a lasting peace.

predictions: Thus/Hence fire clearly; dash items weaker (maybe 0.2-0.4); expect 6-8/8 fire, 0-1 near misses above bar
